copy.byline: A personal archive by Ayush Jain.
copy.statement: Ayush Jain builds full-stack web applications and AI-assisted tools.
copy.intro: I’m Ayush Jain. I build web applications and AI-assisted tools, and study Computer Science at ABES Engineering College. Open a drawer to explore the work, the ideas behind it, and what I’ve learned along the way.
copy.about: I’m a Computer Science student who learns by building. My projects range from small browser tools to retrieval systems, Web3 interfaces, and data dashboards. I’m interested in how a system works beyond its first screen: how information moves, how a decision is explained, and what happens when something fails.
copy.contact: Have a role, a project, or a technical question in mind? Email me with a little context and what you’d like to discuss.

projects.title: Arogya
projects.summary: A healthcare RAG prototype that checks access, evidence, and citations before producing an answer.
projects.problem: In healthcare information retrieval, a confident answer can still be unsafe if its evidence is missing or inaccessible to the reader.
projects.body: Arogya retrieves from a synthetic hospital knowledge base. The pipeline applies role checks, combines lexical and semantic retrieval, considers conflicting or superseded documents, and refuses when evidence is insufficient. Its interface exposes citations and evaluation views. The repository uses synthetic records and is not intended for clinical use.
projects.architecture: React interface → FastAPI pipeline → permission-filtered PostgreSQL evidence → hybrid retrieval and reranking → local generation and citation checks.

projects.title: GenShakti
projects.summary: A renewable-energy planning prototype combining maps, site-selection interfaces, and AI-generated guidance.
projects.problem: Comparing renewable-energy options requires geographic context and an understandable presentation of assumptions.
projects.body: GenShakti brings map-based exploration, energy-planning workflows, and generated recommendations into a React interface. Its source includes mapping and flow-visualization components and a Hugging Face integration. The prototype explores planning interactions; it does not establish measured energy savings or validated site rankings.
projects.architecture: React/Vite browser interface combines map/flow components with external model-service integration.

projects.title: XenoCRM Mini
projects.summary: An engineering-assignment CRM prototype for customer segments, campaign workflows, and AI-assisted planning.
projects.problem: Marketing workflows need customer data, audience rules, campaign actions, and delivery feedback to fit together.
projects.body: The React frontend talks to an Express API backed by Prisma and PostgreSQL. Groq supports AI-assisted campaign interactions. A separate channel stub generates delivery callbacks, allowing campaign state transitions to be demonstrated without claiming real message delivery.
projects.architecture: React/TypeScript client → Express API → Prisma/PostgreSQL; Groq integration and a separate delivery stub with asynchronous callbacks.

projects.title: VigilAI
projects.summary: A retail-analytics challenge project connecting video events to a store-intelligence dashboard.
projects.problem: Store activity is difficult to interpret when detection events, zones, and business views remain disconnected.
projects.body: VigilAI includes a YOLO-based detection pipeline, visitor tracking, zone mapping, event ingestion, and a FastAPI analytics service. A browser dashboard presents funnels, dwell-time views, heatmaps, and anomalies. The project is presented as a challenge prototype; footage rights, identification risks, and metric validity require separate review.
projects.architecture: Video detection/tracking and zone mapping → event ingestion → FastAPI/SQLite analytics, with Redis-supported event transport and a browser dashboard.

projects.title: DevStudy
projects.summary: A developer-learning prototype with code editors, browser previews, and a diagramming workspace.
projects.problem: Learning software development often means moving between code exercises and architecture diagrams.
projects.body: DevStudy combines a Monaco-based editor, web previews, and a Mermaid diagram workspace. The repository describes local execution for web languages and remote execution through Piston for other languages, with a Socket.IO service for battle interactions. Availability of external execution and collaboration services has not been functionally tested.
projects.architecture: Next.js UI combines Monaco and Mermaid workspaces; Piston handles remote-language execution and a separate Socket.IO server supports battle flows.

projects.title: AadhaarPulse
projects.summary: An analytics prototype for exploring district-level Aadhaar authentication patterns and service demand.
projects.problem: Large authentication datasets can hide regional differences in demand and service quality.
projects.body: The dashboard brings maps, district comparisons, demand indicators, and anomaly views into one interface. Python analysis supports the project; the web interface also contains static analytical data. It demonstrates an approach to governance analytics rather than an operational government monitoring service.
projects.architecture: Next.js interface over analytical data exports and static frontend data; Python analysis is separate from the browser application.

projects.title: AI Limit Checker
projects.summary: A Chrome extension prototype for displaying token estimates and usage signals beside AI chats.
projects.problem: Chat interfaces expose different levels of information about context windows and usage limits.
projects.body: Provider-specific adapters collect available page and response information for a floating usage panel. The project combines token estimation, DOM observation, and response interception. Estimates depend on the provider and available signals; they are not authoritative billing or quota measurements.
projects.architecture: Chrome extension adapters → DOM/response signals → token-estimation core and floating interface.

projects.title: ArogyaPlus
projects.summary: A healthcare interface prototype for uploading reports, reading AI explanations, and locating hospitals.
projects.problem: Medical reports often contain terminology that is hard for a patient to interpret.
projects.body: The application connects a report-upload flow to Gemini and presents explanations alongside hospital-map and emergency-summary interfaces. It explores how to make health information easier to navigate. Model output is informational and has not been clinically validated.
projects.architecture: React/Vite interface → Gemini service integration; Leaflet/geolocation and browser storage support hospital-map and emergency-summary views.

projects.title: Calendar Dashboard
projects.summary: A calendar prototype with month views and persisted event creation, editing, and deletion.
projects.problem: Calendar interactions need a consistent link between visual dates, event forms, and stored records.
projects.body: A modular JavaScript frontend drives the main and mini calendars. An Express API stores event records in PostgreSQL. The README describes SQLite, but the server imports pg and the schema uses PostgreSQL features; this record follows the code.
projects.architecture: Modular browser JavaScript → Express event API → PostgreSQL.

projects.title: Employee Management System
projects.summary: A Spring Boot REST API exercise for creating, searching, updating, and deleting employee records.
projects.problem: Managing structured records is a practical way to learn validation and REST API design.
projects.body: The employee controller, service, and repository implement record operations through Spring Data JPA with an H2 database. The archive also contains separate student-management classes; these are not evidence of a larger deployed HR system.
projects.architecture: Spring controller → service → Spring Data JPA repository → H2 database.

projects.title: InFrame Studio
projects.summary: A film-production decision-support prototype for scene risks, location checks, and alternative plans.
projects.problem: Production disruptions can force trade-offs between budget, schedule, and creative intent.
projects.body: The project combines rule-based scoring engines with an Azure OpenAI service integration. Its interfaces present scene analysis and ranked alternative plans. The repository calls the product InFrame Studio, while the deployed page retains VordGuard branding; the record keeps both names as aliases.
projects.architecture: React frontend → Express API → deterministic scoring/decision engines and Azure OpenAI service integration.

projects.title: IPOTrack
projects.summary: An Indian IPO dashboard prototype with listing views, a calendar, charts, and investment calculations.
projects.problem: IPO information is easier to compare when dates, price bands, and subscription figures share one interface.
projects.body: A React frontend presents IPO lists and visualizations. An Express backend includes scraping, caching, and scheduled refresh logic. The website record documents the software design, without presenting scraped figures as independently verified or promising current market data.
projects.architecture: React frontend → Express routes → in-memory cache and scheduled Puppeteer data collection.

projects.title: NyayAI
projects.summary: An AI-assisted legal-document prototype with OCR, plain-language explanations, and speech interfaces.
projects.problem: Legal documents can be difficult to read, especially when technical language and accessibility barriers overlap.
projects.body: The repository defines a React frontend and AWS services for text extraction, language-model explanations, and text-to-speech. Its README explicitly identifies Kiro-assisted creation. This is a software experiment; legal correctness, accessibility conformance, and production readiness have not been independently verified.
projects.architecture: React frontend with AWS Lambda/API Gateway services for Textract, Bedrock and Polly integrations.

projects.title: Placement Tracker
projects.summary: A local-first PWA for tracking placement applications and backing them up as JSON.
projects.problem: Application deadlines, statuses, and notes can become hard to manage across separate documents.
projects.body: The application stores entries in browser storage and includes import/export, deadline reminders, and an installable PWA shell. Local persistence is device-specific; it is not evidence of automatic synchronization between devices.
projects.architecture: Browser interface and service worker with localStorage persistence and JSON import/export.

projects.title: Plant Disease Detector
projects.summary: A browser interface that sends plant photographs to Gemini for suggested disease explanations.
projects.problem: A plant photograph can be difficult to interpret without agricultural expertise.
projects.body: The interface accepts an image and presents a model-generated explanation with treatment and prevention suggestions. Its processing depends on an external model API. The project is an experiment in image-based assistance; the suggestions have not been validated as agricultural diagnoses.
projects.architecture: Static browser interface → Gemini image request → generated explanation display.

projects.title: QueryPDF
projects.summary: A browser-based PDF prototype with local text extraction, questions, summaries, and quizzes.
projects.problem: Exploring a document often requires both reading its pages and asking focused questions about its text.
projects.body: QueryPDF combines PDF.js with a Transformers.js model and a document-viewing interface. The design keeps document processing in the browser after the required assets load. It should be described as a prototype; first-load downloads and browser resource requirements need testing on the target device.
projects.architecture: Browser PDF.js extraction and viewer → client-side Transformers.js model → question, summary and quiz interfaces.

projects.title: Sentinel Agent
projects.summary: A scripted smart-contract security demonstration with exploit tests, a patch flow, and streamed progress.
projects.problem: Explaining a contract vulnerability is more useful when the exploit and corrective change can be followed.
projects.body: The server streams a predefined audit sequence, runs Hardhat tests around a reentrancy example, and replaces the example contract with a checks-effects-interactions version. The reasoning messages and model behaviour are simulated. This demonstrates a workflow, without claiming a general autonomous auditor.
projects.architecture: React dashboard consumes Express SSE events; the server runs a scripted contract/test/patch sequence through Hardhat.

projects.title: Shayoga
projects.summary: A Web3 crowdfunding prototype with campaign browsing, wallet connection, and donation-contract flows.
projects.problem: A crowdfunding interface needs to make campaign details and transaction actions understandable.
projects.body: The project combines React campaign views with Solidity contracts and wallet integration through Ethers.js. It explores campaign creation, progress, and donations in a test-oriented blockchain workflow. The portfolio does not claim verified charitable use, audited contracts, or production fundraising.
projects.architecture: React/Vite campaign interface → Ethers.js wallet integration → Solidity contract functions.

projects.title: SkillForge LMS
projects.summary: A learning-management prototype with course content, enrollment, and separate learner and administrator interfaces.
projects.problem: Course delivery involves both the learner journey and the work of managing structured content.
projects.body: SkillForge separates learner and admin React applications from an Express API. PostgreSQL stores courses and enrollment-related data. The record covers the implemented application structure without claiming an operating education business or verified learner outcomes.
projects.architecture: Separate learner and administrator React applications → Express API → PostgreSQL.

projects.title: Slotly
projects.summary: An appointment-booking assignment with patient and doctor views, availability, and scheduling flows.
projects.problem: Booking interfaces need to connect a patient’s selected time with a doctor’s availability.
projects.body: Slotly uses a React frontend and Neon/PostgreSQL services for account and scheduling flows. The repository contains role-specific screens and booking components. It is an assessment project, without claiming employment at the assessment organization or a deployed clinical service.
projects.architecture: React/Vite role-specific interfaces → Neon authentication/data services → PostgreSQL scheduling records.

projects.title: TaskFlow
projects.summary: A personal-productivity PWA bringing tasks, application tracking, and resource links into one browser workspace.
projects.problem: Tasks and job-application notes are easier to maintain when they share a consistent local workflow.
projects.body: TaskFlow stores user-entered information locally and provides task, application, and resource-link interfaces. Its PWA shell supports installation. The code also contains an external coding-profile proxy, so the portfolio avoids an unconditional claim that no network requests ever occur.
projects.architecture: Browser application and service worker with local persistence; an external coding-profile proxy exists separately.

projects.title: Aurevo
projects.summary: A fashion storefront prototype with product browsing, wishlists, and a shopping bag.
projects.problem: A storefront needs clear product browsing and consistent state between product, wishlist, and cart views.
projects.body: Aurevo explores these flows in a static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript site. Wishlist and shopping-bag state are maintained in the browser. It is an interface prototype; there is no verified payment, fulfilment, or commercial operation.

projects.title: CyberKey
projects.summary: An early JavaScript exercise that generates password strings and copies them to the clipboard.
projects.problem: A small generator is a useful exercise in character selection, string assembly, and clipboard interaction.
projects.body: The page assembles a string from letters, numbers, and symbols and provides a copy action. The source uses Math.random. It demonstrates browser scripting, without making cryptographic security claims.

projects.title: Fusion2048
projects.summary: A browser puzzle game in which matching numbered tiles merge toward 2048.
projects.problem: A small puzzle game brings together state transitions, keyboard input, and visual feedback.
projects.body: Fusion2048 implements tile movement, merging, and score updates in JavaScript. HTML and CSS provide the board and tile presentation. It is an early project in interactive browser programming.

projects.title: Listomo
projects.summary: A small JavaScript task-list application for adding tasks and marking them complete.
projects.problem: A task list is a compact exercise in form handling and visible application state.
projects.body: Listomo presents a focused interface for adding and completing tasks. It belongs with the early browser projects rather than the primary case studies.

projects.title: Media Query Practice
projects.summary: A CSS exercise exploring how a page changes at different viewport widths.
projects.problem: Responsive layout needs explicit rules for different amounts of available space.
projects.body: The exercise uses HTML and CSS media queries to change the page presentation as the viewport narrows. It is retained as early coursework, with no standalone indexable case-study page.

projects.title: SkyLens
projects.summary: A weather-page exercise that looks up a city and displays current-condition fields.
projects.problem: A simple weather interface needs clear search and result feedback.
projects.body: SkyLens uses a browser API request and weather icons to present temperature, humidity, and wind fields. Radar, air-quality monitoring, and forecast accuracy are not supported by the inspected implementation and are omitted.

projects.title: Sustainable Development Dashboard
projects.summary: A static dashboard exercise presenting Sustainable Development Goal indicators with visual score rings.
projects.problem: A dashboard needs a clear hierarchy for presenting scores and comparisons.
projects.body: The project uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to render indicator and chart views. The inspected implementation uses static values. The earlier README’s real-time global-data claims are omitted.

projects.title: Tacwin
projects.summary: A React tic-tac-toe game with turn handling, win feedback, and a reset action.
projects.problem: A small board game provides practice with component state and outcome detection.
projects.body: Tacwin renders the board and alternating moves in React. It presents game results and lets players reset the board. The project is an early frontend exercise; no AI opponent is claimed.

projects.title: UsabilityHub Class Exercise
projects.summary: An HTML and CSS class assignment recreating a marketing-page layout for practice.
projects.problem: Recreating an existing layout can help students learn spacing, page structure, and CSS styling.
projects.body: This exercise recreates the structure of a UsabilityHub page as college coursework. The design and third-party branding are credited to their respective owners. It is not presented as an original product design or a production application.

projects.title: Zenati
projects.summary: An early mental-wellness website prototype with resource pages and chatbot integration.
projects.problem: Wellness information can be difficult to navigate when resources and support options are scattered.
projects.body: Zenati explores a resource-led interface and a chatbot integration. Its forms and self-assessment interfaces are prototypes. There is no verified clinical service, diagnostic capability, staffed callback programme, or donation operation.

projects.title: Aventra
projects.summary: A financial-intelligence project that explores unusual market behaviour and explains the context around a flagged change.
projects.body: The public repository contains a Flask-style backend, market/news service modules, an ML pipeline, and a React frontend. The reviewed intelligence service dispatches analysis jobs. The interface explains market changes; price-prediction accuracy and investment performance are not claimed.

projects.title: Ecofund
projects.summary: A Web3 donation-interface prototype using React and Ethers.js.
projects.body: The inspected client loads a donation ABI and wallet-connected components. The root documentation and checked-in contract are a Hardhat sample, so the deployed contract, end-to-end donation flow, and environmental outcomes are not verified.

projects.title: Finance Categorizer Agent
projects.summary: A browser-based transaction-categorization prototype using explicit rules.
projects.body: The repository separates transaction parsing, category rules, file reading, and evaluation. The inspected categorization core applies rule-table matching; despite the agent name, a language-model integration is not required. Accuracy and Lighthouse badges are source claims and are omitted.

projects.title: Original Portfolio
projects.summary: The earlier Next.js portfolio presenting projects, writing, and professional background.
projects.body: The application uses Next.js, React, and a centralized content file. The Shelf links to this site through the laptop. Its source content is being corrected for the new site; the earlier portfolio is preserved as an original project, without copying its layout.

projects.title: Promptly
projects.summary: A prompt-management interface prototype with version, experiment, and team-workspace screens.
projects.body: The public repository contains a React client with Clerk authentication and dashboard pages. The reviewed prompt and experiment screens use component state, without evidence of a server persistence layer in the returned tree. Version-control, scoring, and multi-tenant service claims in the README are treated as product intentions rather than verified backend capabilities.

projects.title: Amazon Layout Class Exercise
projects.summary: An HTML and CSS coursework exercise recreating an e-commerce homepage layout.
projects.body: The repository contains a static page, stylesheet, and product-image assets. It is retained as coursework, with third-party design attribution and no payment or retail-business claim. Source product images are not copied.

projects.title: ResQHub
projects.summary: A static disaster-preparedness site organizing explanatory pages and resource links.
projects.body: The repository contains pages for disaster types, preparedness, a library, and a map view. It is an information-site exercise, without claiming emergency-response operations. Third-party handbooks remain external source material and are not copied.

projects.title: Web Development Lab — Semester 3
projects.summary: A collection of introductory web-development lab exercises.
projects.body: The public README describes HTML, CSS, and JavaScript coursework. Its frame page responds, but individual exercises were not executed. Keep it in the early-work archive with no standalone indexable page.
